questions.question_text: Which NH statutes govern municipal planning and zoning authority?
questions.explanation: RSA 672 and RSA 674 establish the framework for municipal planning, master plans, and zoning ordinances in New Hampshire. These statutes authorize local governments to regulate land use.

questions.question_text: A developer wants to divide a parcel into five lots. Under RSA 674:35-36, what must the developer obtain?
questions.correct_answer: Plat approval from the planning board
distractors: A special exception from the ZBA
A building permit from the selectmen
questions.explanation: RSA 674:35-36 governs subdivision in New Hampshire and requires plat approval from the local planning board before land can be subdivided into multiple lots.

questions.question_text: A property owner seeks relief from a zoning setback requirement. Which body grants variances?
questions.explanation: The Zoning Board of Adjustment (ZBA) is the local body authorized to grant variances and special exceptions from zoning ordinances under NH land use law.

questions.question_text: A homeowner wants to add a second story to their house in a town that enforces the building code. What approval is required before construction?
questions.explanation: Additions and structural work require a building permit from the local building official. The state building code (RSA 155-A) sets the standards, and RSA 674:51 authorizes municipalities to amend it locally and establish enforcement procedures, including permit and inspection programs.

questions.question_text: A developer applies for both a subdivision plat and a variance for reduced lot sizes. Which bodies must each approve?
questions.correct_answer: Planning board for plat, ZBA for variance
distractors: ZBA for plat, planning board for variance
DES for plat, planning board for variance
questions.explanation: In NH, subdivision plat approval comes from the planning board (RSA 674:35-36), while variances from zoning requirements are granted by the Zoning Board of Adjustment. These are separate bodies with distinct authority.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 482-A, which state agency issues wetlands permits?
questions.explanation: RSA 482-A requires a wetlands permit from the NH Department of Environmental Services (DES) for any dredge, fill, or construction in or adjacent to wetlands.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 483-B, how far does the protected shoreland zone extend from public waters?
questions.explanation: The Shoreland Water Quality Protection Act (RSA 483-B) establishes a protected zone of 250 feet from public waters, 4th-order streams, designated rivers, and tidal waters.

questions.question_text: A buyer wants to build a new house 40 feet from a lake's reference line (natural mean high water level). Is this allowed under RSA 483-B?
questions.correct_answer: No, primary structures must be set back at least 50 feet
distractors: Yes, if a building permit is obtained
Yes, single-family homes are exempt from the setback
No, primary structures are prohibited within 250 feet
questions.explanation: Under RSA 483-B:9, II(b), primary structures must be set back behind the primary building line, which is 50 feet from the reference line. At 40 feet, the proposed house falls within this setback. Small accessory structures such as sheds may be allowed within the waterfront buffer with DES approval if set back at least 20 feet and within size limits (Env-Wq 1405).

questions.question_text: A property owner on porous sand and gravel soil near a lake plans a new septic system. What is the minimum setback from the reference line?
questions.explanation: Septic setbacks under the Shoreland Act vary by soil type. Porous sand and gravel require 125 feet, restrictive layers require 100 feet, and other soils require 75 feet from the reference line. The 75-foot setback also applies from rivers.

questions.question_text: A landowner clear-cuts all natural vegetation 120 feet from a designated river to improve the view. Which RSA 483-B restriction was violated?
questions.correct_answer: Vegetation clearing is restricted within 150 feet
distractors: Clearing is only restricted within 50 feet
No clearing restrictions apply to rivers
questions.explanation: Under RSA 483-B:9, the natural woodland buffer extends 150 feet from the reference line; between 50 and 150 feet, at least 25 percent of the buffer must be maintained as natural woodland, so clear-cutting at 120 feet violates the Act. Impervious surfaces are limited within the full 250-foot protected shoreland.
